chunks: Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no harm in a man giving [the fitrah] on behalf of his dependents while they are absent from him, or ordering them to give on his behalf while he is absent from them," meaning the fitrah (alms of fasting).

key_terms.اَلْفِطْرَة: Fitrah: The alms-tax given at the end of Ramadan to purify the fasting person.
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: His dependents (family members for whom he is responsible).
key_terms.غُيَّبٌ: Absent/Hidden (not present in the same location).

ai.seo_question: Can a man pay the fitrah for his family if they are not present with him?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the flexibility of *fitrah* distribution by permitting proxy payment (*wakalah*) when physical co-presence is impractical. It underscores the Shia juristic principle that the obligation is fulfilled through valid representation, ensuring the poor receive their due even if the payer or recipients are geographically separated.
